C-3 (buy verdicts) and C-4 (expectedReturnPct math, including wiring refiCashSavingsPct into refinance's expectedReturnPct) are separate, not-yet-started PRs per Gabriel's ship-separately decision. Gate: typecheck 0, lint 0, 1874/1882 tests green (8 pre-existing pdf-parse 'bad XRef entry' failures unrelated to this change, confirmed via git stash against unmodified origin/main). Refute-Reviewed: 3-lens adversarial pass (gating-correctness, undrivable-data-edge-cases, regression-and-contract-risk) — 2 CLEAN, 1 confirmed defect (multi-loan LTV/balance basis mismatch) found and fixed with a new regression test (TDD red→green verified). fix-improve-capex-irr-proxy.phase: Phase 5 v2 — improve action / capexIrr proxy (docs/superpowers/specs/2026-06-21-phase-5-capital-allocation-market-intel.md §3.2 rule 3, §15 deferral)
fix-improve-capex-irr-proxy.review_detail: The 'improve' action previously ALWAYS degraded to 'hold' (capitalAction==='invest' branch, v1 stub — no real capex-cost data source exists; src/brain/replacement-cost.ts is scoped to acquisition deals, wrong shape for owned-property capex). Per Gabriel's explicit decision (2026-07-07): build a proxy rather than leave it permanently deferred, and reuse C-4's already-computed general expectedReturnPct (entry value / NOI stream) as the verdict's return figure rather than a separate capex-specific number — a simplification consistent with C-4's own unified redesign (C-4/PR #175 replaced the spec's original per-action expectedReturnFor design with one uniform unlevered-IRR projection). Changes: (1) server/warehouse/capital-allocation.ts — new ASSUMED_CAPEX_PSF=$10/SF [RATIFY] constant (approved default, conservative light-industrial/flex value-add assumption vs. the $125-150/SF REPLACEMENT_COST_PSF ratified for acquisitions); capexIrrEstimate(noiPerSf, sameBasisNoiPerSfMedian) assumes the assumed spend instantly and permanently closes the noiPerSf gap to same-basis peers, checked against hurdleRatePct; gates ONLY action selection. (2) buildVerdict()'s invest branch now fires 'improve' when capexIrr clears hurdle, else degrades to hold with a distinguishing reasons[] message (undrivable vs. doesn't-clear-hurdle). Adversarial refute pass (3 lenses) found 3 real defects, all fixed with TDD regression tests: (a) the capexIrr formula's dimensional soundness as a yield rests on an undocumented load-bearing assumption (instant + perpetual gap closure, no ramp) — now explicitly documented next to [RATIFY], distinguishing it from _projectUnleveredReturn's real multi-year IRR bisection; (b) capexIrr had no structured DataQualityFlag (unlike the expectedReturnPct/basisDiscountPct precedent already established in this file) — added one whenever capexIrr!==null; (c) MOST IMPORTANT — the original median was pooled across ALL properties regardless of basis (cash/accrual/tax/unknown), violating this codebase's own established G3 cross-basis discipline (scores.ts's rankProperties/population partition by basis before comparing NOI/SF) — fixed by computing a same-basis peer median per property (mirroring scores.ts's sameBasis logic exactly, including the unknown-basis-never-pooled rule), recomputed per property rather than once globally. Gate: typecheck 0, lint 0, 2316/2317 tests green (1 pre-existing, unrelated frontend test — comps-view.test.tsx, a date-format assertion, zero diff vs origin/main). Refute-Reviewed: 3-lens adversarial pass (median-and-formula-correctness, gating-and-regression-risk, data-quality-and-transparency) — all 3 found real defects (listed above), all fixed and TDD-verified. PR not yet opened pending Gabriel's go-ahead.

fix-c3-buy-verdicts.phase: Phase 5 v2 — C-3: portfolio-level buy verdicts (docs/superpowers/specs/2026-06-21-phase-5-capital-allocation-market-intel.md §3.5)
fix-c3-buy-verdicts.review_detail: Changes: (1) server/warehouse/capital-allocation.ts — buildBuyVerdict() + a buyable-candidate filter (tier T1/T2, composite>=70, basisDiscountPct null-or->=5% floor) in buildPortfolioAllocation(); emits at most one portfolio-level 'buy' AllocationVerdict for the top-ranked (highest composite, candidateId tie-break) buyable candidate, propertyId='pipeline:<candidateId>'. AllocationVerdict.inputs (healthBand/attentionBand/capitalAction/debtSignal/debtScoreBand/dscr/ltv/noiPerSf) uses documented neutral placeholders with an explicit reasons[] note — NOT extending the schema — per Gabriel's explicit decision (2026-07-07), since a buy verdict isn't tied to an owned property. expectedReturnPct stays null (C-4 deferred). (2) server/warehouse/calibration.ts verdictsFromAllocations() — buy verdicts now tagged subjectKind='deal' (not 'property'), fixing a real defect found in the adversarial refute pass: propertyId='pipeline:...' would otherwise permanently pollute the append-only calibration_verdict log with a subject that resolveDueOutcomes can never resolve. (3) buildBuyVerdict adds a warn-severity DataQualityFlag when the winning candidate's basisDiscountPct is null — found in refute pass: null passes the buyable gate per spec but is indistinguishable between 'genuinely N/A' and 'acquisition score never computed it', so the ambiguity is now surfaced rather than silently invisible. FLAGGED, NOT fixed (out of scope, spec-authored not implementer error): BUY_COMPOSITE_FLOOR=70 (verbatim from spec) diverges from the live acquisition-scoring ruleset's actual T1/T2 bands (config/acquisition-ruleset.v1.json: t1PursueMin=75, t2WatchMin=60) — a T2 candidate scoring 70-74 clears this buy floor despite being well within the T2 band, not near the T1 boundary. This is a ratification-level policy question, not a coding decision — recommend Gabriel either ratifies 70 explicitly as an independent buy-specific floor or has it derived from the live ruleset in a follow-up. Also deliberately NOT implemented (separate, unauthorized scope): spec §3.5's 'RANK all verdicts: attentionBand priority DESC, secondary expectedReturnPct DESC' — verdict ranking is unimplemented in this codebase entirely (not just for buy), pre-dates this PR, and wasn't one of the 3 named deferred items (C-2/C-3/C-4) this session was authorized to fix. Gate: typecheck 0, lint 0, 1879/1887 tests green (8 pre-existing pdf-parse 'bad XRef entry' failures, unrelated). Refute-Reviewed: 3-lens adversarial pass (buyable-filter-correctness, contract-and-downstream-impact, regression-and-scope) — 1 lens fully CLEAN aside from a stale comment (fixed), 2 lenses found real defects (both fixed above, TDD-verified). PR not yet opened pending rebase onto post-C-2 main.

usage.how_to_update: Edit your worktree's entry before starting and after completing work; commit it on your branch. Use ISO 8601 timestamps. Set review_needed=true and fill review_detail when you need architect sign-off on an architect-owned file.
